## Rule

ARC-GEN source: `external/ARC-GEN/tasks/task_3631a71a.py`.

The generator samples colors on the lower triangle of a latent 32x32 square (`trisize=16`),
expands each sampled cell through the full D4 orbit, then clips/draws onto the 30x30
NeuroGolf canvas. The input is the completed output with 2-5 rectangular cutouts changed
to maroon (`9`). The output is the completed 30x30 D4-symmetric canvas.

For a visible coordinate `i`, the latent mirror coordinate is `31-i`; because the canvas is
only 30x30, coordinates 0 and 1 mirror outside the canvas and must map to self. Thus the
usable mirror map is `f(i)=i for i in {0,1}, else 31-i`, implemented as
`[0,1,29,28,...,2]`.

Exact fill uses the full 8-arm orbit:
`(r,c), (r,f(c)), (f(r),c), (f(r),f(c)), (c,r), (f(c),f(r)), (c,f(r)), (f(c),r)`.
Current live uses only the first six arms; it passes visible but misses 140/200000 on the
ARC-GEN truth corpus.

## Algorithm sketch

```python
def solve(grid):
    a = np.array(grid)
    a = np.where(a == 9, 0, a)  # marker 9 contributes no color under orbit Max
    f = [0, 1] + list(range(29, 1, -1))
    return max_over([
        a,
        a[:, f],
        a[f, :],
        a[f, :][:, f],
        a.T,
        a[f, :][:, f].T,
        a[:, f].T,
        a[f, :].T,
    ])
```

The best ONNX variant is now a single output-writing `Einsum`, not the scalar Conv path.
It maps each visible coordinate to a 16-row canonical mirror axis, uses a two-term gate to
sum the normal and transposed D4 halves inside one final node, and masks channel 9 with a
10-value channel vector. Because the only node output is named `output`, the scorer charges
0 activation memory and only the selector params.

The scalar Conv family is still useful as a readable reference: decode one-hot with
weights `[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,0]`, cast to U8, complete the D4 orbit with U8 `Max`, then
write the free graph output with `Equal(filled, channel_ids)` as BOOL.

Floor note: for generator-correct output, the full 8-arm orbit is mandatory. The generator only
requires at least one of all eight latent orbit cells to be visible before drawing, and corpus
case 1828 falsifies the six-arm shortcut. The old scalar-decode family has an immediate lower
bound of 3,600 B Conv decode + 900 B U8 cast + at least one 900 B fill/pre-output canvas, so it
cannot go below 5,400 before doing any real D4 completion. The new final-Einsum avoids that
activation floor entirely: two `[2,16,30]` gates encode "keep ordered pair" vs "swap ordered
pair"; multiplying `keep[t,u,p] * swap[t,u,p]` supplies the input-side canonical fold for both
terms, so no separate `[16,30]` fold initializer is needed.

The 974 form replaces separate keep/swap gates with one fold/ones gate `G[t,u,z]` plus a
2x2 complement selector. The 782 CP form factorizes `G`: `fold - ones/16` has rank 15, so
one all-ones term plus 15 residual row terms reconstruct the gate exactly. It is much slower
than 974, and sub-700 needs a different representation: this gate has exact CP rank 16 and
all 16 canonical rows appear in official examples.

Sign-rank probe: `W = K(p,r)K(q,c)+K(p,c)K(q,r)-tau`. Exact one-hot works, but sub-16D
needs negative off-orbit weights or positive false positives. Official examples immediately fail
from repeated-color suppression, killing the approx-cost 751/691 route.

## Don't-do log

_Record ruled-out hypotheses here so future agents don't retry them._
- Do not call the six-arm orbit generator-correct. It is byte-equal to current live and useful
  as a cost rung, but omits `(c,f(r))` and `(f(c),r)` and misses 140/200000 ARC-GEN truth cases.
- Do not rebuild the final color expansion with OneHot unless a future ORT/scorer change makes
  BOOL Equal invalid. Equal-as-output is cheaper and verified here.
- Do not retry single-half final-Einsum `rect4` or `xpose4` under-2k probes as shippable. Both
  score 1,810 but fail visible 232/267 because each covers only one separable half of the full
  D4 orbit. The correct under-2k route is the two-term gated `einsum_term8_nofold` construction.
- Do not retry two-arm scalar pair probes (`pair_h`, `pair_v`, `pair_t`) as risky submits. They
  do profile under 7k at 6,350, but visible is only 84/267, 88/267, and 66/267.
- Do not try to get sub-700 by dropping canonical CP rows from the final-Einsum gate. All 16
  canonical rows appear with nonzero colors in the official examples; row-truncated gates cannot
  pass visible. Exact CP rank below 16 is also impossible for the fold/ones gate because the
  `t=0` fold slice has matrix rank 16.
- Do not retry low-dimensional sign-rank kernels of the form
  `K(p,r)K(q,c) + K(p,c)K(q,r) - tau` as a risky under-700 submit. Exact 16-D one-hot is fine,
  but 15-D/12-D/11-D embeddings and 10 random d=12/d=11 trials fail the first 20 official pairs
  at 0/20 because repeated colors make negative off-orbit weights unsafe.
- Do not retry sparse `Einsum` selectors without a new scorer mechanism. ORT can run them and
  visible passes, but `score_network_v2`/Gate 5 fail ONNX full_check shape inference with sparse
  input rank 0.
- After the rebased task097 submit failed at 5714.95 public, the preserved `task074_v4` + `task088_v1` staged package SHA `9137BFCFC89EEC4A46CD19728ED2873F4EF85A7E71DCF02E5CDA2D96C20DAD92` became the next queue item again, but submit-captain deferred it pending explicit Bovath approval / policy reconciliation before another credit is spent.
